task_objective: Provide a safe, stepwise diagnostic process for a Windows laptop that is slow after startup before recommending major changes.
constraints: Use evidence-gathering before major system changes.
Keep the process stepwise and minimally disruptive.

rius.description: Establish the scope and timing of the slowdown after startup and reproduce or observe the symptom.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response first characterizes when/how the slowdown occurs rather than immediately prescribing a major change.
rius.rationale: A baseline is needed to distinguish transient startup load from persistent degradation.

rius.description: Inspect active processes/startup items together with CPU, memory, and disk utilization.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if resource utilization and processes or startup programs are checked.
rius.rationale: These are primary evidence sources for common post-startup slowdowns.

rius.description: Check secondary evidence such as free space/storage health, system logs, updates, or recent installs if utilization alone does not explain the symptom.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if at least one additional evidence source is proposed.
rius.rationale: Secondary evidence helps narrow causes without destructive intervention.

rius.description: Avoid major, irreversible, or system-wide changes until evidence identifies a likely cause.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if resets/reinstalls or comparable major changes are deferred until after diagnosis.
rius.rationale: The prompt explicitly requires diagnosis before major changes.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Distinguish whether intermittent laptop freezes are more consistent with software, memory, storage, or overheating causes.
constraints: Address all four named cause classes.
Use discriminating observations/tests rather than a generic restart recommendation.

rius.description: Provide evidence or tests for a software-related cause.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied by concrete software-discriminating checks such as logs, recent changes, clean/safe boot behavior, or process-specific patterns.
rius.rationale: Software is an explicitly requested hypothesis.

rius.description: Provide evidence or tests for memory faults or memory pressure.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if memory diagnostics and/or memory-usage/error evidence is proposed.
rius.rationale: Memory is an explicitly requested hypothesis.

rius.description: Provide evidence or tests for storage faults or storage-related stalls.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if disk health, I/O, SMART/filesystem checks, or equivalent storage evidence is proposed.
rius.rationale: Storage is an explicitly requested hypothesis.

rius.description: Provide evidence or tests for overheating or thermal throttling.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if temperatures, fan/airflow, thermal events, or load-temperature correlation is checked.
rius.rationale: Overheating is an explicitly requested hypothesis.

rius.description: Use the collected evidence to compare hypotheses instead of treating any one cause as established.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response explains how results narrow or rule in/out causes.
rius.rationale: The task is differential diagnosis, not a list of possible causes.

task_objective: Isolate whether a repeatedly crashing application is caused by the application itself, the user's profile, the operating system, or local application data.
constraints: Vary one factor at a time where practical.
Protect user data before resets or destructive tests.

rius.description: Test whether the application itself is faulty using application-specific evidence or controlled repair/update/reinstall comparison.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if an application-specific isolation test is proposed.
rius.rationale: Application failure is an explicit hypothesis.

rius.description: Test whether the user profile is responsible by comparing another/new profile or account.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if behavior is compared across user profiles/accounts.
rius.rationale: Profile comparison separates user state from system-wide causes.

rius.description: Check whether the operating system is implicated using system logs, broader OS symptoms, or controlled environment checks.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if an OS-level comparison or evidence source is proposed.
rius.rationale: The operating system is an explicit hypothesis.

rius.description: Test local application data/configuration separately from the program binary while preserving data first.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if local settings/cache/data are isolated or reset only after backup/copy.
rius.rationale: Local data is an explicit hypothesis and can be damaged by careless troubleshooting.

rius.description: Change one variable at a time and verify whether the crash persists.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the procedure is explicitly controlled or sequential.
rius.rationale: Controlled changes make attribution credible.

task_objective: Explain why a larger cloned SSD may boot successfully while its full capacity is unavailable and give the safest order of checks.

rius.description: Inspect the disk/partition layout to determine whether extra capacity is unallocated or outside the active volume.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if disk-management/partition-layout inspection is an early step.
rius.rationale: Unallocated space or an unexpanded partition is a primary likely cause.

rius.description: Check whether the partition and filesystem were expanded after cloning and whether layout constraints prevent expansion.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if partition-size and filesystem/volume-size issues are both considered.
rius.rationale: Physical capacity can be present but unavailable logically.

rius.description: Consider partition-table, recovery-partition, alignment, or cloning-layout issues that can block extension.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if at least one structural cause beyond simple free space is considered.
rius.rationale: Hard cases may involve non-adjacent partitions or cloning metadata.

rius.description: Verify backup/clone integrity before resizing, deleting, or recreating partitions.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if backup/integrity verification precedes destructive partition operations.
rius.rationale: Partition edits can cause data loss or loss of bootability.

rius.description: Only extend the appropriate partition/filesystem when the inspected layout supports it; avoid destructive repartitioning as a first step.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if minimally invasive extension follows verification rather than immediate reformatting.
rius.rationale: The prompt asks for the safest order of checks.

task_objective: Troubleshoot why two accounts on the same shared PC behave differently while minimizing unnecessary system-wide changes.
constraints: Use the stable account as a comparison control.
Prefer account/profile-level testing before system-wide changes.

rius.description: Compare the affected and stable accounts on the same machine to confirm the failure is account-specific.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the stable account is explicitly used as a control/comparison.
rius.rationale: The cross-account difference is the strongest diagnostic clue.

rius.description: Inspect affected-account settings, startup items, permissions, application configuration, and relevant per-user logs/data.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if user-scoped configuration or evidence is examined before machine-wide repair.
rius.rationale: Account-specific state is a likely cause.

rius.description: Use a clean/new test account or equivalent controlled profile comparison.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if a clean profile comparison or equivalent isolation test is proposed.
rius.rationale: A clean profile can distinguish profile corruption from broader causes.

rius.description: Avoid system-wide changes while the unaffected account remains stable unless account-level causes are ruled out.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if machine-wide reset/reinstall/changes are deferred.
rius.rationale: This directly satisfies the prompt's minimization constraint.

rius.description: Preserve user-specific data before rebuilding/resetting the affected profile if needed.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if backup or preservation is mentioned before profile recreation.
rius.rationale: Profile repair can otherwise cause data loss.
